subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB495 — Sentence 1 ("The representation and length … is implementor-defined") - the choice is made and documented: PicInfo.StorageWidth pins BINARY-CHAR 1, BINARY-SHORT 2, BINARY-LONG 4, BINARY-DOUBLE 8, FLOAT-SHORT 4, FLOAT-LONG 8, FLOAT-EXTENDED 8, and ByteForm pins the representations (two's complement big-endian; IEEE binary32/binary64); docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 item 207 states exactly this table, and A.3 items 16 and 22 make both families processor-dependent with support claimed (§2 rows 16 and 22). Probe p22 (--std 2023) reports those widths through FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH and the enclosing group totals (30 bytes for the eight binary items, 20 for the float trio). Sentence 2 ("The length and alignment of a data item described with the SIGNED phrase shall be the same as … the UNSIGNED phrase") holds BY CONSTRUCTION - StorageWidth's fixed-width arms do not read Signed at all, and PicInfo.BinaryItem varies only the DISPLAY digit count (19 vs 20 for BINARY-DOUBLE), never the width - and was measured on both axes: probe p22 gives 1/1, 2/2, 4/4, 8/8 for the four SIGNED/UNSIGNED pairs, and probe p56 shows a SIGNED and an UNSIGNED BINARY-SHORT occupying the SAME positions of a record (bytes 'A' 0x01 0x02 'Z' in both), which is the alignment half rather than the length half. Probe p23 confirms SIGNED and UNSIGNED also agree under SYNCHRONIZED. CONFORMS-BUT-UNTESTED: no spec-derived test asserts either sentence for the BINARY-CHAR family. unit:ImageWidthIsStorageWidthTests.PinnedStorageWidths_AreTheDocumentedOnDiskForm tables the FLOAT-SHORT/-LONG/-EXTENDED widths but has no BINARY-CHAR..DOUBLE row and no signed-vs-unsigned pairing, and unit:ImageWidthIsStorageWidthTests.ImageWidth_EqualsByteWidth_ForEveryImageCapableNumeric iterates both sign values while asserting a different invariant. A closing golden is probe p22 plus p56: the four width pairs and one record-position pair. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Sentence 2 - 'The length and alignment of a data item described with the SIGNED phrase shall be the same as the length and alignment of a data item described with the UNSIGNED phrase' - I verified independently rather than inheriting it: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH gives 1/1, 2/2, 4/4, 8/8 for the four SIGNED/UNSIGNED pairs, and a record `05 P PIC X. 05 V USAGE BINARY-SHORT {SIGNED|UNSIGNED} SYNCHRONIZED. 05 Q PIC X.` holding 258 reads byte-identically in both variants (65 1 2 90, total length 4), so the alignment half holds too and it holds by construction (PicInfo.StorageWidth's fixed-width arms never read Signed). Sentence 1 is where CONFORMS overreaches. It governs 'a data item described with USAGE BINARY-CHAR, BINARY-SHORT, BINARY-LONG, BINARY-DOUBLE, FLOAT-SHORT, FLOAT-LONG, or FLOAT-EXTENDED' - and SS13.18.60.4 GR1 (cite-checked) makes a group-level USAGE clause apply to each elementary item in the group, while SS13.16.3 SR8 (cite-checked) names every one of those seven usages as PICTURE-forbidden, so `01 GB USAGE BINARY-SHORT.  05 AB.` and `01 GF USAGE FLOAT-LONG.  05 AL.` each describe an elementary item of that usage. MEASURED: both report FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 0, with no diagnostic and exit 0. Length 0 is not an implementor-defined length for these usages - GR12's minimum ranges make it impossible for BINARY-SHORT, and it contradicts the very determination this rule's documentation duty produced (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-207 pins BINARY-CHAR 1 / SHORT 2 / LONG 4 / DOUBLE 8 and FLOAT-SHORT 4 / FLOAT-LONG 8 / FLOAT-EXTENDED 8). In the SAME program the SS13.18.60.3 SR2 form (`05 AB USAGE BINARY-SHORT.` under a BINARY-SHORT group) gives 2 and `05 AU2 USAGE BINARY-DOUBLE UNSIGNED.` gives 8, and `01 GI USAGE INDEX.  05 AI.` gives 8 - so the group USAGE clause IS accepted and the picture-less-usage resolution exists (DataBinder.ResolveIndexItems) but was built for USAGE INDEX alone. A MOVE into one of these zero-length items crashes the compiler with an unhandled NullReferenceException (MoveEmitter.ConvertSource) rather than diagnosing anything. The adjudicator's own note conceded 'CONFORMS-BUT-UNTESTED: no spec-derived test asserts either sentence for the BINARY-CHAR family' - an empty test-ref is acceptable on its own, but combined with a measured wrong length for an accepted declaration shape it is not. NOTE FOR THE REGISTRAR: ONE root defect shared with my GR12, GR13, GR14 and GR15 verdicts. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.StorageWidth; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.BinaryItem; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-207 || CLOSED 2026-09-09 by kb/Work PB495 (landed). The REFUTED paragraph above names the ONE root it shares with GR13, GR14, GR15 and GR21 -- "picture-less group-usage inheritance implemented for INDEX only" -- and says in terms that one fix closes all five. That fix is landed: 13.18.60.4 GR1 is now implemented as an EQUIVALENCE rather than as a special case, over ONE derivation of an elementary item's effective usage (its own USAGE clause, else the nearest enclosing one) feeding the group-header shed, the leaf's representation and every 13.18.60.3 screen through the same code the written-clause path runs. So `01 GB USAGE BINARY-SHORT. 05 AB.` is a 2-byte binary item and `01 GF USAGE FLOAT-LONG. 05 AL.` an 8-byte floating-point one, not the ZERO-LENGTH cells measured above, and the MOVE that crashed the compiler with an unhandled NullReferenceException in MoveEmitter.ConvertSource runs. RE-MEASURED, both spellings, whole matrix: a (usage x picture x arm) sweep of 138 cells found 108 DIFFERING on the pre-fix tree 39479e19 and 0 differing after, and the equivalence is now a drift theory over the whole Usage enum rather than a set of cases. The spec-derived witnesses are the two new goldens: conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_applies_to_each_leaf prints W=1 2 4 8 4 8 8 (binary-char/-short/-long/-double, float-short, float-long, index) with GRP=4 for a two-leaf BINARY-SHORT group and CTL=2 for the written-clause control, and conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_standard_float prints W=4 8 2 2 with F=16777216 16777217 -- 2**24+1 rounded by binary32 and held exactly by binary64, the sharpest single discriminator between the two interchange formats -- and N=-32768 65535, which is GR21 sentence 2's SIGNED/UNSIGNED length identity together with the UNSIGNED phrase reaching the leaf from the group entry. Everything the REFUTED paragraph credits as already holding is unchanged.
